title: Which big data tool fits you?

questions.q: What is the main job you need done?
questions.hint: Big data has four jobs: store, move, process and query. Pick the one that hurts most.

options.label: Store large files
options.why: you need a place to keep files

options.label: Share a stream of events between systems
options.why: many systems must read the same events

options.label: Crunch data in big batches or streams
Copy database tables into a lake
options.why: you need to load database data into Iceberg or Parquet

questions.hint: Free software still has a bill: servers and the person who gets paged at 2 a.m.

options.label: My team runs them
options.why: you have staff to run clusters

options.label: I want a vendor to run them
options.why: you want no cluster to babysit

questions.q: How fresh do results need to be?

options.label: Batches every few minutes or hours are fine
On our own hardware
options.why: you must keep everything on your own machines

options.why: you are already on Google Cloud

questions.hint: Cloud tools bill differently: bytes scanned, credits or DBUs.

options.label: I know the bytes my queries read
options.why: per-TiB billing is easy to forecast for you

hadoop.name: Apache Hadoop (HDFS)
hadoop.summary: Free software for storing and batch processing huge files on your own servers.
hadoop.bestWhen: you run your own cluster and your jobs are large batch jobs.
hadoop.watchOut: HDFS favors high throughput over low latency, so it is not for quick, interactive answers.

s3.name: Amazon S3
s3.summary: AWS file storage where you pay for what you store and run no cluster.
s3.bestWhen: you want storage you do not operate yourself.
s3.watchOut: it stores files and does not process or query them, and requests and data transfer out bill separately.

kafka.name: Apache Kafka
kafka.summary: An event streaming platform that stores events so many systems can read them.
kafka.bestWhen: several systems must publish and read the same events.
kafka.watchOut: database import goes through Kafka Connect, a separate part, and managed Kafka comes from various vendors.

spark.name: Apache Spark
spark.summary: One engine for big batch jobs, SQL and machine learning.
spark.bestWhen: you have large batch jobs, or want SQL and machine learning in one place.
spark.watchOut: the Spark news page lists July 2026 releases on four lines, so check which one your connectors and cloud support.

flink.name: Apache Flink
flink.summary: A stream processing engine that remembers earlier events while new ones arrive.
flink.bestWhen: results must update within moments of an event.
flink.watchOut: you upgrade on its support schedule, since the community supports the current and previous minor release.

trino.name: Trino
trino.summary: A SQL query engine that reads data where it already sits.
trino.bestWhen: your data is already in files and you want SQL over it without loading it elsewhere.
trino.watchOut: it is not designed for OLTP, meaning many small app-style reads and writes, and you run the servers.

bigquery.name: Google BigQuery
bigquery.summary: A serverless warehouse on Google Cloud with a free first TiB of queries each month.
bigquery.bestWhen: you already live in Google Cloud and want no cluster to manage.
bigquery.watchOut: the on-demand bill follows data scanned, so big full-table queries cost real money, and the Google docs we read show no self-hosted option.

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: An open-source tool (Apache 2.0) that copies database tables into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on storage you control.
olake.bestWhen: your data starts in a database such as Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server or Oracle and you want it in a lake.
olake.watchOut: it loads data rather than querying it, so pair it with an Iceberg catalog and a query engine.

snowflake_databricks.name: Snowflake or Databricks
snowflake_databricks.summary: Managed platforms billed by compute: Snowflake in credits, Databricks in DBUs.
snowflake_databricks.bestWhen: you want a managed warehouse (Snowflake) or managed jobs and SQL together (Databricks), and can estimate hours of compute.
snowflake_databricks.watchOut: credit prices vary by region, and Databricks DBUs per hour were not on the pages we read.
